Miss Nadia and I are the only ones who know what we talked about in that conversation on that famous Friday.
How she spoke to me as soon as she picked up the phone, how I spoke to her, and everything else, unless her memory is failing her.

And ego and the inability to accept that someone isn't doing something right prevents you from improving at your job.
It's clear you're not going to agree, but deep down I think you don't like criticism or anyone getting angry. Maybe you need everyone to adore you and tell you how good you are.
It's up to you.

And I'm not going to give very specific details of that famous conversation.
We'd have a problem.

And you wouldn't be interested anyway, because you might lose one client, but you'd gain others.

I've been trusting this veterinary clinic for seven years, and I couldn't be more grateful for the care we've always received.

From the very first moment, it's clear they're passionate about their work and that the animals' well-being is their top priority. They are highly professional, friendly, attentive, and always make you feel that your pets are in the best hands.

After all these years, I can say with complete confidence that they will continue to be my trusted veterinary clinic. Thank you for taking such good care of my furry friends and for the dedication you put into your work every single day.
It's run by Nadia; you can see her love for animals and people, she's so sweet, she knows what she's doing.

The best vet in Valencia. They saved my Jackye and I'm eternally grateful. They are very professional and even better people, with exceptional character.

I accompanied my brother to have his faithful companion euthanized after a long and difficult journey. A sarcoma had left the poor animal with no other options. I want to congratulate Dr. Nadia, who was incredibly kind and gentle throughout, bringing peace to the animal. I was deeply moved. My sincerest congratulations; the staff were absolutely wonderful.

My trusted vet, the one I've always gone to.
The way they treat both the animals and their owners is excellent; they always take personal needs into account and make everything easier. They're always available for anything, which gives you a lot of peace of mind.

Highly recommended! They treat the animals incredibly well, with great calm, gentleness, and kindness. They explain everything clearly and without rushing. Excellent value for money. They avoid unnecessary treatments and carefully consider all the options. I'm very happy with them.
The best vet I've ever taken my pets to. I recommend her to anyone who needs it.
Delighted with the service.

They couldn't be kinder or more professional.
Nadia's care for Nuca is exactly what we all want for our little ones. The surgery went perfectly, and the post-operative support, affection, and professionalism were outstanding.
I'm so grateful to everyone at Veterinario San Pedro because they are incredibly kind, knowledgeable, and thoroughly explain your pet's condition and the available solutions so you can make an informed decision.
Thank you for treating Nuca so well; you are definitely a top-notch team.
I would like to thank the entire team, and especially Nadia, for their kindness during a difficult time. Thank you for your final gesture, which we will always cherish. Thank you for your support.

I recommend this place not only for its professionalism but also for the heart they put into everything they do. Thank you, ladies, for helping us say goodbye with dignity and love.

Responding to Alicia P.'s comment on my first review: Either your memory is failing you, or you're trying to whitewash your image by lying. Go ahead, but I predict you'll fail. My habit of keeping everything works in my favor. I have reports, lab results, and ultrasounds from you, as well as Darko and Derek's complete medical records from your hospital. EVERYTHING, including screenshots (with dates) from the website where I mentioned that you wanted to amputate Darko's ear due to an aural hematoma and that I was advised to use Trombocid. How dare you claim you told me that? Don't play games with my honor, and I won't allow you to tarnish it. I can expose your lie by uploading the screenshots. If you claimed the idea of ​​using Trombocid to put it in his medical record, the dates will speak for themselves.
Derek was born in October 2008. I brought him to you when he was very small in 2009. Darko was older, and we left the vet who was treating him to bring both of them to you. Because of proximity.
From 2009 to 2013 is 4 years, not 5. I've been at a good hospital for eleven years. My other 3 cats and my dog ​​are still there. That says it all.
In 4 years with you, many visits, yes, vaccinations, deworming, Darko's skin issues, an ear infection, and Derek's urinary problems: UTIs, cystitis, nothing atypical in some unneutered male cats. Antibiotics and castration resolved it, and he never suffered from it again.
Castration that stands out for your inefficiency in not seeing the testicle in the groin.

So tell me, what are Derek's MANY HEALTH PROBLEMS, besides the temporary urinary ones? Because he never had glomerulonephritis. At your hospital, they never saw it. Another mistake on your part. I'm so glad I didn't want to go to that nephrologist in Gandía.
Then came the matter of Darko's aural hematoma. You drained the blood from his ear several times, and it kept coming back. You operated on him twice, and not because of poor healing; his ear would swell again shortly after, which is why you operated on him. Stop lying. Surgeries, anesthesia, suffering for him. You also deny saying that if it came back, the solution was to cut off his ear? Do you think I would have allowed that? You put him through all that, and you have the nerve to say that you recommended Trombocid to me? Are you saying that you wanted to get money from me, knowing the solution and operating unnecessarily? Terrible, immoral. You're exposing yourself by choosing to lie.
Ma'am, the fact that my husband took Darko for a vaccination in 2012 indicates that we weren't unhappy? What a ridiculous way to justify yourself! The worst came in 2013 when the truly serious problems appeared. How dangerous. That's why I decided to leave. After Derek's diagnosis of HCM by the cardiologist, which I NEVER doubted, you ignored my reasoning about the medication and refused to admit that he did NOT have tachycardia at HOME. I was right.
Tarsicio (the cardiologist) discontinued his medication (bless him) and I never saw you again. Derek arrived at the new hospital with slightly low blood pressure and mild dehydration, having gone 24 hours without beta-blockers or diuretics.
They repeated everything. NO pericarditis, very MILD HCM, normal sinus rhythm, slightly tilted heart. And in his 16 years, the HCM never progressed. Without treatment or symptoms. Regarding Darko's laryngeal edema, which you mistook for tracheitis, you ramble about medications you prescribed to evade your mistake. They inserted a camera and saw the edema, they treated it, you DID NOT.
You're still on the same track.
And mind you, my husband took him to you without my approval because of the blessed proximity and his haste. But that's where he ended up with you too.
A good veterinarian carries GREAT responsibility, efficiency, commitment, work ethic, and even professional intuition. Nobody is God; some diseases are incurable, but that wasn't Derek's case, although in your hands he wouldn't have lived a happy 16 years, that much is clear. Nor would Darko have lived 15. Regarding that debt you mentioned, I neither doubt nor confirm it. I know nothing about it. Is this how you're trying to make me look bad? Pathetic. My husband was the last one to go. Talk to him. And you NEVER called me, don't lie. I would have answered to tell you all this.
In MY opinion, you were a mediocre and incompetent veterinarian. I have the right to say so, and I have said it, and I hope it helps someone like me.
Fantastic treatment of the animals. Delighted with this veterinary center.

Thank you so much, Javier, for your review! It's always a pleasure to serve you and your pets. We're here for anything you need!
Best regards and Happy New Year!
San Pedro Veterinary Center

San Pedro brings back very bad memories, all involving Alicia P. I'm sure she'll remember me if she reads this. I've wanted to write this review for years, in case it's helpful to anyone.

Her first mistake, let's say a minor one, was during the castration of my cat, a wonderful, sweet Ragdoll. She anesthetized him without palpating his scrotum first, and once he was asleep, she saw that he was missing a testicle. She performed an ultrasound but was unable to find the testicle, and my cat received anesthesia for nothing since she canceled the castration. The next day, she scheduled an appointment with an ultrasound technician who immediately found the testicle in his groin. Shame on you, Alicia; you should palpate first to check for cryptorchidism.
One day, my dog, a Golden Retriever, developed an aural hematoma on his ear. She operated on him, and it came back. She performed another surgery and told me that if it came back again, his ear would have to be amputated. She dragged him out on a blanket and left him in the waiting room, lying there on the floor. My dog ​​wouldn't wake up and had to be given an antidote. He had a terrible awakening. I consulted another vet and they told me that applying Thrombocid would clear it up. So when it came back, I applied it for a week and it disappeared completely. It never came back. She looked incredulous when I told her. She would have cut off his ear, and the solution was an ointment.
Here's where things get more serious.
When my cat was five years old, he was diagnosed with heart disease via echocardiogram (which I requested). A cardiologist came to the clinic and performed the test. He was prescribed a diuretic and a beta-blocker. As soon as he started the treatment, my cat began to live only to urinate and sleep; literally, he barely ate.
I kept insisting on how worried I was about the treatment and how my cat was suffering the effects, and she kept telling me I shouldn't stop it because without it, he could die. We had a bit of an argument because she insisted my cat had tachycardia at rest, and I maintained that he didn't, that he only had it at the clinic due to stress. I even recorded his heartbeat at home with a stethoscope and microphone and played it for her, but she wouldn't listen. So I got the phone number of the cardiologist who performed the echocardiogram and explained how weak my cat was. He gave me an email address to send the audio recording of the heartbeat, and when he heard it, he agreed with me and told me to stop the treatment immediately. My cat's behavior returned to normal.

I remember she said he didn't have much time and that if I let him run around, he could have a heart attack.
Alicia, you should know that he's been living a normal life, running daily, jumping, climbing, playing a lot, and without medication. It turned out to be a very mild case of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), without pericardial fluid. Just annual checkups at a good hospital.
The last thing was a misdiagnosis with my dog. Although I already had another vet, my husband insisted on taking him. According to Alicia, he had tracheitis, and she started medicating him without any tests. My dog ​​was breathing terribly, noisy, mute, and barely eating, and she just kept increasing the medication dosage. Common sense dictates that when a treatment isn't effective, the diagnosis is incorrect, and persisting is a waste of time, sometimes vital.
My new vet ran tests, and it turned out to be more serious than tracheitis; it was a large laryngeal edema that prevented him from swallowing, barking, or even breathing. He improved quickly with the right treatment. That's when all contact with Sanpedro ended. This woman's behavior was one mistake after another, marked by negligence, a lack of professionalism, and a complete lack of cooperation. It's so important to listen to the owner; the information we provide is invaluable in guiding the vet. Getting them out of there saved their lives. My dog ​​lived happily for 15 years. He passed away peacefully in 2016, at a very old age, with both ears intact.

My cat lived a healthy, happy, and wonderful life for 16 years, which is a long time for a Ragdoll. Sadly, I lost him this October 2024 to kidney failure due to old age, not from HCM.
I have four other animals—three cats and a dog—and I would never leave them in her care, even if she were as close as crossing the street.
